item.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Tethered Jailbreak Uses OpenAI Codex and SmileBASIC 4
item.description:
Nintendo Switch 2 Tethered Jailbreak Uses OpenAI Codex and SmileBASIC 4

A Nintendo Switch 2 console has been jailbroken, and a modder demonstrated a custom Mario Kart World with new playable characters using a software‑only, tethered exploit that leverages an older game and OpenAI’s Codex.

🔍 Overview

  • The Switch 2 jailbreak is software‑only and tethered, meaning it must be launched from a game each time the console powers on.
  • A modder ran a custom version of Mario Kart World featuring Cinnamoroll, the red Angry Bird, Peter Griffin, and Steve from Minecraft.
  • The exploit was created with the assistance of OpenAI’s Codex, referred to as the “ns2jb” jailbreak.
  • The exploit is built around the game SmileBASIC 4, which lets users program and play games (though another modder says the title is “not strictly needed”).

🧩 How it Works

  • An older game (SmileBASIC 4) is used as the launch point for the jailbreak.
  • OpenAI Codex contributed code that enables the “ns2jb” jailbreak.
  • Because the jailbreak is tethered, the user must run it from the game every time the console is turned on.
  • The method does not modify hardware; it operates entirely in software.

🎮 Custom Content

Character Source
Cinnamoroll Sanrio
Red Angry Bird Angry Birds
Peter Griffin Family Guy
Steve Minecraft

⚙️ Key Details

  • Software‑only: No hardware changes are required.
  • Tethered: Must be executed from a game on each boot.
  • Required game: SmileBASIC 4 (though its necessity is disputed by another modder).
  • AI involvement: OpenAI’s Codex was used to develop the jailbreak code.

#NintendoSwitch2 #jailbreak #OpenAI #Codex

Source: Someone hacked the Switch 2 by using an old game and AI

item.title: RTX Spark laptops combine Arm CPU, Blackwell GPU and unified memory for AI agents
item.description:
RTX Spark laptops combine Arm CPU, Blackwell GPU and unified memory for AI agents

Microsoft and Nvidia held a launch party for the first wave of RTX Spark laptops last week in San Francisco, where a new wave of AI PCs took center stage amid a packed crowd and a lively hands‑on area.

🔍 Overview

  • RTX Spark is a new class of Windows laptops that pairs an Arm‑based CPU with Nvidia’s Blackwell GPU and a unified‑memory architecture.
  • The design enables powerful AI models to run locally on a laptop, making the experience of setting up an AI agent quick and easy.

🧩 Architecture & Core Tech

  • The chips inside RTX Spark laptops are Arm‑based, instead of the traditional x64 architecture used by AMD and Intel.
  • Microsoft’s Prism emulator is used for apps that don’t have a native Arm version.
  • “Each core is different. How we translate x64 to that core needs to be highly optimized, and for RTX Spark we’ve done a lot of work to optimize for its microarchitecture.” – Peter Dawoud

⚙️ Features

  • Get Started experience: “When users get into Windows for the first time, they’ll see a new Get Started experience that will launch on an RTX Spark laptop that allows them to find the agent they want, get started with that agent, install it, and get to that agent in only two clicks,” says Peter Dawoud.
  • Agent installation: Agents can be installed and updated through the Windows Store, eliminating the need to track dependencies.
  • First‑party agents: Hermes, Perplexity, and OpenClaw are the first three officially supported agents at launch.
  • Unified memory: Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra can ship with up to 128 GB of unified memory, making it possible to load huge models into memory.
  • “We made incredible investments in Unified Memory Architecture to enable you to load as much as possible into the 128GB,” says Dawoud.
  • Memory optimizations cover power, performance, battery life, and allow a game to run while rendering a video in the background.
  • Memory slider: A slider in Nvidia’s Windows app lets users manually adjust how much of the unified memory is dedicated to the GPU side. This is useful on RTX Spark laptops with 24 GB or 32 GB of memory to balance more to the GPU for particular apps and games.
  • Gaming capability: While RTX Spark laptops aren’t marketed as gaming machines, they can run the latest AAA titles. Anti‑cheat support was secured as a first step for gaming on Windows on Arm.

Supported AI Agents

Agent Status at launch
Hermes Officially supported
Perplexity Officially supported
OpenClaw Officially supported

Games with Built‑in Anti‑Cheat Support

Game Anti‑cheat support
Fortnite Supported out of the box
Marvel Rivals Supported out of the box
Arc Raiders Supported out of the box
Counter‑Strike 2 Supported out of the box
Dota 2 Supported out of the box

🚀 Availability

The first wave of RTX Spark laptops was unveiled at the San Francisco launch event. Microsoft and Nvidia are continuing to work with additional anti‑cheat providers to bring more games to the platform in the future.

💡 Why it matters

  • Combining an Arm CPU, Blackwell GPU, and up to 128 GB of unified memory lets laptops load and run large AI models locally.
  • The streamlined Windows Get Started flow reduces the steps needed to find, install, and launch an AI agent to just two clicks.
  • Unified‑memory tuning and a manual slider give users flexibility to balance performance for AI workloads and gaming on the same device.

#RTXSpark #AIagents #ArmPC #UnifiedMemory

Source: How Windows is being optimized for Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptops

item.title: Epic Games previews AI‑assisted, faster launcher with Linux support
item.description:
Epic Games previews AI‑assisted, faster launcher with Linux support

Epic Games announced today a preview of a refreshed Epic Games Launcher that is “way faster” and adds Linux support.

🔍 Overview

  • The new launcher is described as “way faster” and “more responsive than the current one, and has a new look.”
  • It now supports Linux alongside Windows and Mac.
  • Epic says the refresh was “vibe coded.”

🛠️ AI involvement

  • Epic has been “making a big push into AI‑assisted development,” and this approach includes the new launcher.
  • Martin Keely, Epic’s VP and GM of the Epic Games Store and Epic Online Services, said “We used AI as a tool for this.”
  • AI has been “super helpful” for testing and for “replicating the core functionality from the existing launcher.”
  • Keely added that AI also enabled offering the launcher on Linux.
  • The team “definitely had agents write and review all of the code,” and “used it to replicate the core functionality.”
  • The development process was “managed that process” and “supervised the entirety of what we did.”
  • While the team has not adopted the “no more hand‑written code” model reported by Bloomberg, the effort “is on the same train” as the company’s broader AI pivot.

🚀 Availability

  • The new Epic Games Launcher preview is available on Windows, Mac, and Linux beginning today; the old version will remain available.
  • Epic also announced plans to bring Fortnite to Linux through the app.
  • No specific timeline for a full migration; Keely says the full launch will happen when the update feels “stable” and has parity in “all places that we need” with the current launcher.

📈 Why it matters

  • CEO Tim Sweeney announced a “huge pivot underway” to “move developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration.”
  • He emphasized the goal is “not to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.”
  • Sweeney noted the recent March layoffs of more than 1,000 staffers are “not related to AI,” and added, “To the extent it improves productivity, we want to have as many awesome developers developing great content and tech as we can.”

#EpicGames #AIdevelopment #LinuxGaming

Source: Epic’s new games launcher is ‘vibe coded’

item.title: Microsoft Launches Xbox Labs to Explore AI‑Driven Game Modding
item.description:
Microsoft Launches Xbox Labs to Explore AI‑Driven Game Modding

Microsoft announced a new Xbox Labs group to experiment with AI‑powered decompilation and recompilation of games, turning emerging ideas into experiences for players and developers.

🔍 Overview

  • Xbox Labs is described as “a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience.” – Xbox CEO Asha Sharma
  • The group will focus on rapid emergence of mods that use AI models to remix games in ways rarely seen before.
  • Microsoft has already seen mods such as skateboarding added to Call of Duty and Halo running in a web browser.

🤖 AI in Game Modding

  • AI models are helping modders decompile, recompile, and merge code from different titles.
  • Sharma notes that “coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software,” and that games share many of those same properties.
  • Players spend more than 72 billion hours a year on Xbox games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide.
  • Microsoft plans to share any tools and learnings from Xbox Labs with the broader developer community.

⚙️ Experiments & Findings

  • Recent weeks have seen classic PC builds translated to run on Apple Silicon and ported to browsers via WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90 % global browser support.
  • Modders are achieving results similar to Microsoft’s Xbox backward‑compatibility program—running old games on modern hardware—without the business‑model restrictions Microsoft traditionally faces.
  • Some of the largest games have been remixed into the source code of another, challenging long‑held assumptions about the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games.

💡 Why It Matters

  • “While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co‑creators.” – Sharma
  • These outcomes benefit players even when they challenge existing business models.
  • The work hints at a future where modern games could be decoupled from their intended hardware, potentially just “a model or two away” from further breakthroughs.

⚖️ Legal & IP Considerations

  • The rapid decompile‑and‑recompile activity raises questions about unauthorized use of Microsoft’s IP.
  • The company did not comment on potential IP violations before publication.
  • While modding is “fun,” there is uncertainty about how publishers will react if modern console games appear where they shouldn’t.

#Xbox #AI #GameModding #Microsoft

Source: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports

item.title: Dwarf Fortress Developer Tarn Adams Adopts Version Control After Years Without It
item.description:
Dwarf Fortress Developer Tarn Adams Adopts Version Control After Years Without It

Dwarf Fortress creator Tarn Adams has adopted version control tools, bringing an end to years of developing the game’s complex codebase without source control.

🔍 Overview

Despite the inherent complexity of the Dwarf Fortress codebase, the project ran for years without version control. Statements from creator Tarn Adams trace how his approach to source control shifted over a decade of development.

⚙️ Key details

Tarn Adams commented on his use of version control across three distinct periods:

  • March 2013: “I don’t use version control – I didn’t like the feeling of having the code get committed into a black box thingy with no immediate upside”
  • March 2016: “I don’t even use version control. If you don’t know what that is then you’re not gonna yell at me. If you even know what version control is you’re gonna be like, ‘You don’t use version control? You don’t use source control? What is wrong with you? How can you even work? I’m just not cut out for it, in a sense. It’s been 15 years, so the reasons have change over time, but that’s my current understanding of it.”
  • March 2023: “I’ve got Discord channels to check and version control stuff to use now, so the process is definitely a little more involved”

💡 Why it matters

The March 2023 update was shared during an interview about the Steam release of Dwarf Fortress, which made the developers millionaires. The transition marks the adoption of version control tools and Discord channels into their active workflow.

#DwarfFortress #VersionControl #GameDev #SoftwareEngineering

Source: Dwarf Fortress uses version control now

item.title: GPT-6 Astra Autonomously Beats Portal in 23-Hour Session
item.description:
GPT-6 Astra Autonomously Beats Portal in 23-Hour Session

GPT-6 Astra has beat the game Portal autonomously. The task was completed in 23 hours using thousands of individual decisions and visual screenshots.

🔍 Overview

The model functioned independently to navigate the game’s environment without manual guidance. This autonomous performance relied on visual inputs and sequential decisions to progress through the game from start to finish.
